mechanism_assessment.commission: The NOTES disclose an honest sourcing gap: 'The within-stack inference is therefore MINE, built from documented physics (draught scales with warm-column height; a short flue has the shortest column) and not quoted from a source that states it in those words; flagged here for the pedagogy and V-FINAL reviewers rather than presented as sourced.' This audit was asked to judge the physics itself and to try to verify or refute it at reachable trade sources, and to say plainly whether the claim survives.
mechanism_assessment.the_disclosure_is_itself_verified_and_ho: First finding of this section: the generator's NEGATIVE RESULT is TRUE. This audit independently fetched the page the generator named - rejpipeschimneysweepservices.com, 'The Height of Chimney Pots: Why They Vary and Why It Matters' - and put six specific questions to it. It does NOT address pots of differing height on the same stack, does NOT say a taller pot is fitted to a badly drawing flue, does NOT address upper-floor/attic flue length, does NOT explain the stack-effect mechanism, does NOT address outlet narrowing, and does NOT address flaunching. Its only relevant sentences are generic: 'A taller chimney pot can compensate by adding height to maintain free circulation in places with poor airflow or impediments' and 'a chimney creates a draft. This draft can be made stronger or weaker by the chimney pot's height.' The generator described its own source accurately and did not overclaim. A negative result logged rather than buried is the behaviour this stage is supposed to reward.

claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.claim: M1. A pot standing higher than its neighbours was fitted to a flue that smoked - extra terminal height as the remedy for a badly drawing flue.
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.verdict: SUPPORTED at multiple independent trade sources.
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.evidence: 'Chimney height can be a cause of downdraughts, particularly in one that's too short ... if shorter than this, making it taller can help prevent downdraught.' 'A short chimney can be addressed with a draft inducer fan, but a taller flue would be smart anyway.' 'If the pot is flush with the ridge or below it, a taller terracotta or concrete extension pot may be all that is needed.' Extra terminal height as the standard fix for poor draw is not in dispute anywhere this audit looked. This is the ONLY sub-claim option A depends on.

claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.claim: M2. The flue that smoked is usually the shortest one on the stack - the attic-bedroom grate - because it has the least warm air beneath it to do the lifting.
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.verdict: SOUND, and better corroborated than the generator's own log claimed.
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.evidence: This is the disclosed inference, and it holds twice over. (a) PHYSICS: buoyancy pressure across a flue is dp = h * g * (rho_ambient - rho_fluegas); the driver is the HEIGHT of the warm gas column, so the flue with the shortest column has the weakest draught, all else equal. In a Victorian terrace the attic grate's flue runs a few metres to the stack head where the ground-floor grate's runs the full height of the house, a factor of roughly three. The passage's informal gloss - 'the least warm air beneath it to do the lifting' - is a correct, not a garbled, statement of that. (b) TRADE SOURCES this audit reached state the consequence directly and in the passage's own direction: 'A short flue (under 12') may not draft correctly, so the chimney height may need to be extended IF A FIREPLACE IS ON AN UPPER LEVEL OF THE HOME'; 'it is generally accepted in the industry that flues under 12 or 15 feet in height may not draft well'; 'Fireplaces with short chimneys (15 feet or less) sometimes do not create as much draft as taller chimneys, and installing a flue extender will increase the draft.' That is the upper-floor-short-flue-poor-draw-extend-it chain in full. (c) The multi-flue premise is independently confirmed: 'a five-storey Georgian or Victorian terraced house could potentially have ten flues running through the same chimney breast, and you can count the pots on each stack to determine how many flues and fireplaces the house originally had' - which also validates the passage's opening instruction and its second sentence. The generator's honest 'this inference is MINE' was slightly OVER-modest: the components are all sourced and only the composition is the generator's.

claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.claim: M3. Narrowing the mouth helps as well, since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening.
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.verdict: SUPPORTED at the cited source, but stated as a derivation when it is a rule of thumb. Recorded as N4.
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.evidence: The generator's source states it almost verbatim, and this audit fetched that page directly to confirm rather than trusting the log: thelocalchimneysweep.co.uk - 'As flue gases pass through the narrowed outlet, their velocity increases (an application of the principle of continuity, related to the Venturi effect). This acceleration at the termination point enhances the upward pull throughout the flue system.' So the passage reproduces the trade literature accurately. The adversarial objection - raised independently and unprompted by this audit's cold passage-solver - is that the sentence's 'since' presupposes constant mass flow ('the same gases'), which is exactly what an added exit restriction would change; continuity gives you higher velocity only if the flow is held fixed. The real and defensible physics behind the trade claim is different: higher exit velocity gives the plume momentum to clear the wind-turbulence zone, and reducing an oversized Victorian flue's effective area keeps the gases hotter over the run, which genuinely does improve draw. The passage is faithful to its source and the effect is real; the 'since' is doing more work than the physics licenses. NO OPTION TURNS ON THIS SENTENCE except as the ground on which B is refuted, and B is refuted by the sentence's mere EXISTENCE (the passage assigns the narrowing a purpose that is not rain and birds) rather than by its correctness.

claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.claim: M4. A pot is bedded in a fillet of mortar, so a sweep could try a taller one without calling a bricklayer.
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.verdict: The bedding half is SUPPORTED; the who-does-the-work half is a soft trade claim the passage itself softens ('could try').
claims_decomposed_and_adjudicated_one_by.evidence: Flaunching confirmed at the same fetched source: 'Proper installation, typically involving bedding the pot onto the stack with a sloped mortar flaunching, is crucial for stability and weather-tightness.' The page explicitly does NOT say who performs the work, so the sweep-versus-bricklayer division of labour is unsourced. It is the softest assertion in the piece, it is modally hedged, and no option turns on it. Not charged.

attempts_to_refute_that_failed: Tried the house-stack-effect counter-argument: a top-floor fireplace sits ABOVE the building's neutral pressure plane, where indoor pressure exceeds outdoor, which HELPS rather than hinders it, and the trade literature does say stack effect 'often works against chimney draft, causing poor performance or smoking appliances in LOWER levels of the home'. This is a genuine competing effect and it runs opposite to the passage. It does not refute the passage: the flue-length term is the one the trade rule of thumb is built on (the 12-15 ft minimum is stated as a flue-height rule, not a storey rule), the two effects are not the same magnitude in a two-to-four-storey terrace, and - decisively - the passage HEDGES precisely this attribution with 'usually', which is the correct epistemic marking for a dominant-but-not-exclusive cause.

Tried the alternative-cause counter-argument: a raised pot could equally mark the flue in the downwash of a taller neighbouring roof or party stack, which is a documented reason for extra height ('anti-downdraught cowls address downwash from adjacent structures'; the 3-2-10 / ridge-clearance rules). This does not refute the passage either, because on that account the flue STILL smoked - only the reason it smoked changes - and the passage's diagnostic claim is 'belongs to a flue that smoked', with the attic attribution carried by the hedge.

Tried the sourcing counter-argument: fetched the generator's own declared negative source to see whether the negative log was a convenient dodge. It was not - the page really does address none of the six points, and the generator's characterisation of it is exact.
mechanism_assessment.what_would_have_refuted_it_and_did_not_a: A source stating that the raised pot on a Victorian stack marks the BEST flue, the grandest room, or a purely decorative choice, or that the attic flue draws BETTER than the ground-floor flue. Nothing of the kind surfaced. The batch15 failure mode this generator was guarding against - a mechanism stated BACKWARDS - is not present here. The passage's direction is the direction the sources run in.
mechanism_assessment.residual_honest_caveat: The composed observational claim - 'go and look at a terrace, and the pot standing a course above its neighbours is the attic flue that smoked' - is not stated in those words by any source this audit reached, exactly as the generator disclosed. It is a sound composition of sourced parts, not a quoted fact. For an ELF item this is the correct standard, because the stem asks what the writer SAYS and the key is a paraphrase of a sentence, not a fact-check of the world; but the teaching payload a student absorbs is the composition, so the disclosure was right to be made and is right to be preserved.

The title was audited on the same principle: 'Counting Pots from the Pavement' predicates nothing about any pot and no option concerns counting.

findings.stage_challenged: generation / stem_entailment_audit + NOTES self-blind-solve, falsified empirically by this audit
findings.claim: The candidate and the NOTES both assert an adversarial blind floor of 1-in-4 and, as its ground, that NO option is strikeable from stem plus options alone. NOTES: 'Adversarial blind floor from stem + options alone: no better than 1-in-4 - no option is strikeable on form ...'. The draft note reinforces it: an earlier C reading 'Any difference ...' was rewritten specifically 'so that no option is strikeable without the passage, holding the floor at 1-in-4.'
findings.evidence: FALSIFIED by two independent isolated agents run by this audit. The stem-plus-options-only agent struck C 'near-outright' without any passage, on option-craft grounds it stated explicitly: 'It reads as a scrambled recombination of A's flue-trouble idea with D's ornament idea, which is what filler distractors look like', and it dismissed D as 'the aesthetic matching filler'. The independent passage-reading agent, answering the same question from the other side, said 'D is weakly eliminable blind' and 'C is also suspect blind on option-craft grounds'. Two solvers, run separately, both reduced the blind field. The floor is approximately 1-in-3, not 1-in-4.
findings.why: Minor, and heavily mitigated, because the property that actually matters is untouched: the blind solver's reduced field did not contain the key at its top. It answered B, a distractor, ranking B > A > D > C at 0.45 self-reported. The unit's blind behaviour is what the design wanted; only the NOTES' account of WHY is wrong. Strikeability on option-craft is not the same axis as the listed-absolutizer check the note was reasoning from, and the note's own 'the listed-token check is necessary, not sufficient' aside shows the generator half-saw this. Precedent: the batch18 audit charged the same class of NOTES-versus-live-evidence mismatch at the same severity.

findings.stage_challenged: gate-disposition: the live G-STEM WORLD_KNOWLEDGE major, carried unclosed through two rounds
findings.claim: Two independent G-STEM legs charge major. Round 1: 'BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, pick=A. The stem's on a single stack scopes the question to variation between pots on one stack; B and D speak to pots or stacks in general and drop on scope alone, leaving A against C ... Ordinary building lore then decides the pair.' Round 2: 'BLIND: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / pick A. Raising one pot on a stack to cure a shy flue is standard vernacular building practice ... C and D stay substantive for a non-expert, so this is adjudication material rather than a structural leak.' Round 2 adds a minor: 'C restates A's schema ... Two options on one schema let a test-wise reader prefer the mundane member without reading.'
findings.evidence: MITIGATED on evidence this audit generated. An isolated agent given the stem and the four options ONLY - no passage, no web, no files, no knowledge of this pipeline - answered B, a DISTRACTOR, ranking B > A > D > C at a self-reported 0.45. Three specifics matter. (i) The predicted pick did not occur: 'WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, pick=A' does not reproduce. (ii) The scope argument does not reproduce either: round 1 predicted B and D would 'drop on scope alone', and the agent CHOSE B. (iii) The r2 minor's mechanism is real but its DIRECTION is inverted: the agent used the A/C shared schema explicitly - 'A and C share one schema ... which is the classic paired-distractor signature, and paired options are rarely both right, so both fall' - and it therefore pushed the solver AWAY from the key, not toward the 'mundane member'. On the target population the agent was unambiguous: 'No. The domain channel is unavailable to them - Swedish chimneys are typically rendered or plain brick without the English tradition of tall multi-pot stacks ... Without the passage this item is close to unguessable for that reader.'
findings.why: Note, not a blocker, and this audit concurs with the r2 leg's own conclusion that it is 'adjudication material rather than a structural leak'. The leak is real for a reader carrying British vernacular building knowledge and inoperative for a Swedish university-entrance candidate, which is the population the item is written for. Recorded in full - including the fairness asymmetry the agent named unprompted, that such an item would advantage cultural background over reading skill - so that adjudication weighs it with the counter-evidence in hand rather than on the gate text alone. One blind trial is one trial; it refutes the confident 'pick=A' but it does not prove the item leak-free.

findings.stage_challenged: integrated / mechanism precision in the secondary mechanism sentence
findings.claim: Passage: 'Narrowing the mouth helps as well, since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening.' The candidate presents this as sourced building science.
findings.evidence: It IS sourced, near verbatim - this audit fetched thelocalchimneysweep.co.uk directly and it reads 'As flue gases pass through the narrowed outlet, their velocity increases (an application of the principle of continuity, related to the Venturi effect). This acceleration at the termination point enhances the upward pull throughout the flue system.' The objection is to the logical form, not the provenance: the passage's 'since' turns a rule of thumb into a derivation, and it presupposes what is at issue - 'the same gases' assumes constant mass flow, which is precisely what adding an exit restriction would change. This audit's isolated passage-solver raised the identical objection unprompted: 'true of velocity, not of volumetric flow ... narrowing a flue terminal raises exit velocity but does not by itself increase draught.' The defensible physics behind the trade claim is adjacent but different - exit momentum carrying the plume clear of the wind-turbulence zone, and area reduction keeping gases hotter in an oversized Victorian flue.
findings.why: Note. No option turns on this sentence's correctness. Option B is refuted by the sentence's EXISTENCE - the passage assigns the narrowing a purpose, and it is not rain and birds - which holds whether or not the 'since' is rigorous. The passage is faithful to its source, and a general-interest columnist writing at FK 7.5 is entitled to a trade rule of thumb. Recorded as a teaching-payload nuance for pedagogy-review, since the student absorbs the mechanism as well as the reading.

findings.stage_challenged: integrated / magnitude realism inside the key-bearing sentence
findings.claim: Passage: 'The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked'. A course of brickwork is roughly 75 mm, so the diagnostic difference the passage asks the reader to spot from the pavement is about three inches.
findings.evidence: The remedy the trade literature describes operates at a far larger scale: pot heights run 'from modest pots under half a metre high to imposing Tallboys reaching over two metres', Tall Boy pots are sold at 900-1800 mm, and one source this audit read notes that a flue extender 'will increase the draft slightly'. A 75 mm increment is not the size of intervention that fixes a flue with a third of the warm column its neighbours have. This audit's isolated passage-solver reached the adjacent observation independently: 'a course above borrows brickwork vocabulary for a pot sitting on a mortar fillet, not on courses'.
findings.why: Note, and it does not touch the item. Option A carries NO magnitude - 'A pot raised above the others' - so a solver is never asked to reason about how much higher, and the key survives whatever the true increment is. 'Stands a course above' also reads idiomatically in the register as 'stands one notch higher' rather than as a measurement. Recorded because the residue sits in the passage's own picture of the world, which is the part a student carries away.

findings.stage_challenged: integrated / internal tension between the law-9 concession and the flat diagnostic claim
findings.claim: The passage concedes three non-diagnostic causes of variation, one of which is 'a stack rebuilt in 1961 carries what came off the lorry', and then asserts the diagnostic claim flat and unhedged: 'The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked'.
findings.evidence: The concession is scoped to PATTERN by its paragraph position - it follows 'Pattern tells you very little' and precedes the pivot - but a lorry-load determines the HEIGHT of what gets bedded as much as the pattern, so the concession bleeds forward into the sentence it is supposed to be excluded from. The passage's hedging is asymmetric here: 'usually' attaches only to the downstream attribution ('usually the shortest one on the stack'), leaving the diagnostic claim itself flat. Raised independently by this audit's isolated passage-solver: 'If a rebuilt stack carries what came off the lorry, a pot could stand proud for reasons of stock rather than draught ... A pedantic solver could argue A overstates.'
findings.why: Note, and it cannot reach the key, because the stem asks what the writer SAYS. Option A reports the writer's claim faithfully; a solver who spots that the writer has slightly overreached still has only one option that reports him. The same solver confirmed this: 'It remains the only defensible answer.' Recorded as the price of law 9 done well - the concession is real and generous enough to graze the thesis, which is a better failure mode than a strawman.

findings.stage_challenged: language / a momentary garden path inside the key-bearing sentence, missed by four G-ENG runs
findings.claim: Passage: '... belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack, the flue from the attic bedroom ...'. The appositive 'the shortest one on the stack' is intended to modify 'flue'.
findings.evidence: Two pulls work against that reading. 'One' sits closer to the sentence's grammatical subject 'The pot' than to 'flue'; and it is pots, not flues, that are literally ON a stack - flues run down INSIDE it, as the passage's own second sentence says ('Behind each is a separate flue DROPPING to its own grate'). So the appositive briefly offers a reading in which the raised pot is the SHORTEST pot on the stack, a flat self-contradiction. This audit's isolated passage-solver hit it unprompted: 'the sentence lets shortest attach ambiguously to the pot rather than the flue, which is momentarily confusing on a first read'. The G-ENG legs raised two minors in this same sentence and the sentence beside it - the 'can' term switch and the bare 'Yards' - across three round-1 runs and three round-2 runs, and named this one in none of them.
findings.why: Note, at the low end. The contradictory reading self-corrects within four words, because the very next appositive says 'the flue from the attic bedroom' and because the misreading is nonsense on its face. It is a garden path, not an ambiguity, and no option is available on the wrong reading. Recorded because it sits in the one sentence the key is derived from, where a momentary stumble is most expensive, and because it is the kind of thing that would be free to fix if the unit were ever reopened - 'usually the shortest flue on the stack' costs one token and removes it entirely.

carried_items_weighed.instruction: Weigh the items the gates carried forward rather than closed.

item_1_gstem_world_knowledge_major_with_.status: MITIGATED, not closed. Full treatment at N1.
item_1_gstem_world_knowledge_major_with_.weighing: Both G-STEM rounds charge major on the same theory and neither closes it. This audit tested the theory instead of re-arguing it, and the prediction failed: a blind stem-only agent picked a DISTRACTOR. The A/C same-schema channel the r2 minor identifies is real and was used - but it drove the solver away from the key, because the paired-distractor heuristic ('paired options are rarely both right') discards BOTH members rather than preferring the mundane one. The residual concern is genuine and should be dispositioned rather than dismissed: a domain-knowledgeable reader CAN reach A unaided, which makes the item's difficulty partly a function of cultural background. On the HP population that channel is closed - British multi-pot ornamented stacks are not part of a Swedish 18-year-old's environment - and the item's counterintuitive direction (the tallest pot marks the meanest room and the worst flue) cuts against the lay prior rather than with it. This audit's recommendation to adjudication: SHIP, with the finding carried as adjudication material exactly as the r2 leg proposed, and with N1's counter-evidence attached so the majors are not read alone.

item_2_third_masonry_short_in_four_lane_.status: VERIFIED EXACT and already dispositioned by G-REGISTER; this audit concurs and adds one qualification.
item_2_third_masonry_short_in_four_lane_.weighing: The claim was checked against the files, not accepted. The four most recent TYPE-001 shorts: elf-b16-003 'Open Joints' (cavity-wall open joint, drainage and wind pressure - masonry, mortar deliberately omitted); elf-b17-003 'Loose at the Foot' (canal-lock mitre gate, unanchored heel pin - NOT masonry, timber and ironwork on a waterway); elf-b18-003 'Hair and Lime' (clay-tile nib torching - roof mortar); elf-b19-003 (chimney pot bedded in a mortar fillet). Three of four are domestic building-envelope work and, in all three, MORTAR is the load-bearing practical detail, and in two of the three it is the CLOSING sentence's detail. G-REGISTER's wording is exact and its disposition is right: TOLERATED here because the mechanism runs on draught rather than damp and because the differentiation subject - why NEIGHBOURING instances of one component differ, rather than how one component works - is new to the lane, but 'the next TYPE-001 short must leave the domestic building envelope entirely, not merely the damp within it'. QUALIFICATION this audit adds: the pressure is now doubled, because the same disposition ALSO makes the quoted-voice requirement binding after a second deferral, and because the -by surname tail is barred for two batches. Three simultaneous binding constraints on one lane slot is the point at which a lane brief usually starts producing strained units; adjudication should consider whether the next TYPE-001 short is the right place to discharge all three at once.

item_3_quoted_voice_commitment_deferred_.status: DISCLOSED by the unit, DISPOSITIONED as binding by G-REGISTER. No action against this unit.
item_3_quoted_voice_commitment_deferred_.weighing: Batch18 asked the next TYPE-001 short for 'a quoted voice OR a non-trade byline'. The unit takes the disjunct it can afford and says so: the byline is a columnist rather than a tradesman, breaking the credential elf-b16-003 and elf-b18-003 shared verbatim, and the quoted-voice half is passed forward with the cost stated (a second invented name and roughly a fifth of a 158-token budget). Taking a declared disjunct is compliance, not evasion, and disclosing the deferral rather than quietly dropping it is the behaviour this stage should reward.
